subject: Unexpected embeddings token surge — request for billing clarification
messages:
From: Alex Morris <alex@orbitai.com>
To: billing@redwood.ai, logan.wright@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 05 Oct 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Spike in embeddings token count on 2027-10-04

Hi team —

We noticed a large unexpected jump in embeddings token billing for our account on 2027-10-04 (line items attached). Our daily run should produce ~120k embedding tokens; the invoice shows a 9x spike. We run batched embedding calls from a worker that dedupes IDs upstream, so it's surprising. Can someone confirm if the metering changed (e.g., per-request vs per-embedding attribution) or if there's a known double-count edge case for long CSV batch uploads?

I've attached a short usage sample and a session trace from our worker for 2027-10-04. We'd like a quick sanity check and, if this is an accounting error, a request for a corrective credit.

Thanks,
Alex Morris
Head of Platform
OrbitAI

Attachments: orbitai-embeddings-usage-sample.csv, orbitai-session-trace-20271004.json

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morris <alex@orbitai.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 05 Oct 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in embeddings token count on 2027-10-04

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the signal and for attaching the samples. I pulled the high-level telemetry and see the same spike on our side for your account between 03:20–03:40 UTC on 2027-10-04. Two quick notes:

- We have no platform-wide metering policy change recorded that day.
- Preliminary traces show a pattern that can happen when a client retries with an overlapping batch id and the request-level attribution breaks into individual embedding attributions (counts each vector). That can multiply token accounting when dedup isn't applied consistently before the call.

I'm looping in Marissa (billing) to validate the invoice and Jordan (SRE/ingest) to review the session trace you provided. Can you also confirm whether the worker retries on 5xx / connection timeouts and whether you send the same batch id header? A screenshot of your job scheduler logs for 03:15–04:00 UTC would help.

I'll follow up with a proposed short-term credit if this is a metering duplication.

Best,
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Alex Morris <alex@orbitai.com>
Cc: jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 05 Oct 2027 13:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in embeddings token count on 2027-10-04

Alex / team —

I reviewed the invoice lines and matched the high-cost requests to the session timestamps Logan mentioned. The items in question appear under the embeddings endpoint with repeated request_ids from the same client key. Before we propose a credit, we need Jordan to confirm whether the duplicate request_ids are client-side retries or server-side replays. If client retries produced duplicate attributions, standard practice is to issue a partial credit for the duplicate window. I've drafted a provisional worksheet (attached) estimating a 70% credit on the additional token consumption while we investigate.

If OrbitAI can provide scheduler logs showing an external retry flood, we can expedite the credit. Otherwise, we'll run a deeper log correlation.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed-credit-worksheet.xlsx

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Alex Morris <alex@orbitai.com>
Date: Wed, 06 Oct 2027 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in embeddings token count on 2027-10-04

Alex — pulled your session trace and correlated it with our ingestion logs. Notes below (abridged):

- At 03:21:14 UTC we saw a burst of POST /v1/embeddings requests from your API key with identical batch_uuid headers for ~780 separate calls across 2 minutes.
- Our runtime attribution path for batching normally aggregates by batch_uuid but falls back to per-vector attribution if the batch metadata is missing/partial. Several of the requests from your trace lacked the batch metadata payload due to a truncated body on retry, which triggered the fallback.
- We do not see server-side replays for your key; the calls were accepted as unique requests.

Recommended next steps:
1) We can issue a provisional billing credit for the duplicated portion (Jordan->Marissa: compute 55% of the overage for now) while OrbitAI confirms retry behavior.
2) Fix: I'll add a guard in the ingest path to reject requests that declare a batch_uuid but present incomplete metadata during the 30-day probe window; that change will prevent this class of fallback overcount for future runs.

Logan / Marissa: if you approve the provisional credit I will produce the evidence export for the billing adjustment.

—Jordan
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morris <alex@orbitai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 07 Oct 2027 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in embeddings token count on 2027-10-04

Alex —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for sending the scheduler logs earlier this morning. Based on Jordan's correlation, we agree this was a client-side retry pattern that resulted in partial metadata loss and triggered per-vector fallback counting. Marissa has provisionally approved a credit equal to 55% of the delta consumption for 2027-10-04 while we complete a 7-day audit window.

What to expect next:
- Marissa will apply the provisional credit to your October invoice within 3 business days.
- Jordan will deliver the evidence export (ingest traces + attribution keys) and a short postmortem on the guard change.
- We'll include a small account-level best-practice note for batching and retries to help OrbitAI avoid repeats.

If that plan works, say "Ack" and we'll proceed. Appreciate the quick collaboration.

Best,
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
